newsitem.title: USA: Niagara Mohawk rate case again extended.
newsitem.headline: Niagara Mohawk rate case again extended.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp said Tuesday it agreed to a request by the New York Public Service Commission staff for a two-week extension of the company's 1997 rate request proceedings.
Without another extension, staff and intervenor testimony in the case would have been due Tuesday, the utility noted.
But one intervenor, the New York State Consumer Protection Board, filed Monday with the Public Service Commission recommending denial of the requested electric rate increase.
Five previous extensions in the case have been granted to allow parties to focus on issues related to Niagara Mohawk's PowerChoice proposal, the utility noted.
The company said it is continuing negotiations toward a settlement on PowerChoice, which is expected to eliminate the need for the rate proceeding.
Last week, spokesman Nicholas Ashooh said the negotiations are with independent power producers, seeking an end to government-mandated contracts to purchase their electricity.
"We've got to solve (the problem of non-regulated power costs) before we can move on with PowerChoice," he said.

In February 1996, the company filed for an 8.4 percent average rate increase to become effective January 1, 1997, due in part to the rising cost of power it must continue to buy from unregulated generators if PowerChoice is not achieved.
With a two week extension, Nimo said, the effective date of the requested rate increase is August 22, 1997.
The utility had no comment Tuesday on the Consumer Protection Board's request that the rate increase be denied.
